non_claims: Primary, secondary, benzylic and alicyclic sulfates are not told apart.
The number of sulfate groups is not claimed; only mono-sulfate hypotheses are tried.

notes: measure:false, provisional (WS0 2026-11-19, pending the author): the SO3 radical anion is HSO4- minus OH, so HSO4- with the SO3 radical anion is one parent-daughter channel; HSO4- with HSO3- or the SO3 loss would be two ions.

competitors.note: Aryl sulfates can show weak HSO4- (Correia 2020: 4-hydroxybenzoic and syringic acid sulfates, 5 %); p-cresyl sulfate is an isomer of benzyl sulfate.
H2PO4- and the HPO3 loss sit 9.5 mDa from HSO4- and the SO3 loss; the p2 product tolerance and the observed-precursor loss reference keep them apart.

priors.note: Only mono-sulfate [M-H]- hypotheses are tried: bis-sulfates ionise mainly as [M-2H]2-, a charge state outside the v1 format.

terms.note: HSO4- must exceed both the SO3 loss ion and the SO3 radical anion (dominant HSO4-); HSO4- 96.9601 lies 9.5 mDa from H2PO4- 96.9696, outside the p2 product tolerance of 5 mDa at this m/z.
SO3 radical anion 79.9574; in [M-H]- of a non-aryl sulfate only for benzyl alcohol sulfate (Correia 2020 Table 1); McLeod 2017 shows it with HSO4- for steroid bis-sulfate dianions.

SO3 79.9568 lost from the observed precursor beside a strong HSO4- in mandelic and phenyllactic acid sulfates (Correia 2020 Table 1); the HPO3 loss (9.5 mDa heavier) falls outside the product tolerance.
